title: Talking about landscape painting
description: Natural beginner conversations for talking about being a landscape painter, describing your work, and answering common questions about painting.

acceptedTranslations: I am a painter.
I'm an artist.
notes: Use « pintora » if the speaker is a woman.

acceptedTranslations: I paint landscape paintings.
notes: « Paisaje » means landscape; « paisajes » is the plural.

lessons.english: What kind of painting do you do?
acceptedTranslations: What kind of paintings do you make?
What kind of art do you make?
notes: A natural informal question about someone's work.

acceptedTranslations: I mainly paint landscapes.
Mostly, I paint landscapes.
notes: « Sobre todo » means mainly, mostly, or above all.

acceptedTranslations: I like to paint nature.
notes: « Me gusta + infinitive » is a very useful way to talk about activities you enjoy.

acceptedTranslations: Do you paint with oil paint?
Do you use oils?
notes: « Al óleo » means in oils or with oil paint.

acceptedTranslations: No, I use acrylic paint.
No, I paint in acrylics.
notes: « Pintar con acrílicos » is a natural way to describe using acrylic paints.

acceptedTranslations: Do you paint outside?
Do you paint in the open air?
notes: « Al aire libre » means outdoors.

lessons.english: I usually paint in my studio.
acceptedTranslations: Normally I paint in my studio.
I generally paint in my studio.
notes: « Normalmente » is a common way to describe what you usually do.

acceptedTranslations: Sometimes I paint outdoors.
notes: « A veces » means sometimes.

acceptedTranslations: I also work with photos.
I use photos too.
notes: In context, « trabajar con fotos » can naturally mean using photographs as references.

lessons.english: I take a lot of photos when I travel.
acceptedTranslations: I take lots of photos when I travel.
notes: « Tomar fotos » is widely used throughout Latin America.

lessons.sentence: Busco lugares que me gustaría pintar.
lessons.english: I look for places I'd like to paint.
acceptedTranslations: I look for places that I would like to paint.
notes: A useful phrase for explaining how travel and painting fit together.

lessons.sentence: Me gusta mucho la luz de aquí.
lessons.english: I really like the light here.
acceptedTranslations: I like the light here a lot.
notes: A simple, natural comment for an artist talking about a place.

acceptedTranslations: The sky is incredible today.
The sky looks amazing today.
notes: A natural conversational observation about the landscape.

acceptedTranslations: I really love those trees.
notes: « Me encanta » and « me encantan » are very common ways to express strong liking.

lessons.sentence: Este lugar sería bonito para pintar.
lessons.english: This would be a beautiful place to paint.
acceptedTranslations: This would be a nice place to paint.
This place would be beautiful to paint.
notes: « Sería » means would be and is useful for expressing an idea or possibility.

lessons.sentence: ¿Cuánto tiempo tardas en pintar un cuadro?
lessons.english: How long does it take you to paint a painting?
acceptedTranslations: How long does it take you to paint a picture?
How long do you take to paint a painting?
notes: « Tardar en + infinitive » is a useful construction for talking about how long something takes.

acceptedTranslations: Normally, a few hours.
Usually it takes a few hours.
notes: A natural short response to a question about duration.

acceptedTranslations: Which part is your favorite?
What's the part you like best?
notes: A broadly useful question that works naturally when discussing a painting.

lessons.sentence: Me gusta mucho pintar el cielo.
lessons.english: I really like painting the sky.
acceptedTranslations: I really like to paint the sky.
I enjoy painting the sky a lot.
notes: Another natural use of « me gusta + infinitive ».

lessons.sentence: Para mí, la luz es muy importante.
lessons.english: For me, light is very important.
acceptedTranslations: Light is very important to me.
notes: « Para mí » is a useful way to introduce a personal opinion.

lessons.english: I use lots of different colors.
acceptedTranslations: I use many different colors.
I work with lots of different colors.
notes: « Usar » is a simple and useful verb when describing materials or technique.

acceptedTranslations: Do you sell your artwork?
Do you sell your pictures?
notes: « Cuadro » commonly refers to a painting as a finished artwork.

lessons.english: Yes, I make a living from my painting.
acceptedTranslations: Yes, I make my living as a painter.
Yes, I earn my living from painting.
notes: « Vivir de algo » means to make a living from something.
